name: Pete Dye Stadium Course
description: Pete Dye's desert stadium course, all railroad ties, deep pot bunkers and water, finishing with the island-green 17th.

name: Torrey Pines Golf Course (South Course)
description: A long municipal layout on the cliffs above the Pacific, home of two U.S. Opens and some of the Tour's toughest par 4s.

name: Pebble Beach Golf Links
description: Golf's great seaside stage: small greens, the tiny 7th over the rocks, and an 18th that hugs Carmel Bay.

name: TPC Scottsdale (Stadium Course)
description: The Stadium Course in the Sonoran Desert, famous for the raucous amphitheater around the par-3 16th.

name: The Riviera Country Club
description: George C. Thomas's classic in a Pacific Palisades canyon, with kikuyu rough, the short 10th and the bunker in the middle of the 6th green.

name: PGA National - Champion Course
description: A Florida test defined by the Bear Trap, the water-lined stretch from 15 through 17.

name: Trump National Doral - Blue Monster Course
description: A long, flat Miami layout with water in play on most holes and a notorious lakeside 18th.

name: TPC Sawgrass - THE PLAYERS Stadium Course
description: Pete Dye's stadium original and home of THE PLAYERS, where every round builds to the island-green 17th.

name: Arnold Palmer's Bay Hill Club & Lodge
description: Arnold Palmer's Orlando club: long par 4s, firm greens and water on the closing hole.

name: Memorial Park Golf Course
description: A public course in the heart of Houston, renovated by Tom Doak with wide fairways and severe, tightly mown runoffs.

name: TPC San Antonio - The Oaks Course
description: A Greg Norman design carved through Texas Hill Country oaks, often played in a stiff wind.

name: Augusta National Golf Club
description: Alister MacKenzie and Bobby Jones's masterpiece of azaleas, pines and fast greens, and the stretch through Amen Corner.

name: Harbour Town Golf Links
description: Pete Dye's tight, tree-lined lowcountry links with tiny greens, ending at the lighthouse on Calibogue Sound.

name: TPC Louisiana
description: A Pete Dye course in the bayou outside New Orleans, flat and windy, with waste areas and water throughout.

name: TPC Craig Ranch
description: A modern North Texas parkland course with generous fairways that rewards aggressive scoring.

name: Innisbrook Resort - Copperhead Course
description: A rolling, pine-lined Florida course where the round ends on the Snake Pit, 16 through 18.

name: Quail Hollow Club
description: A long, demanding Charlotte club that finishes on the Green Mile, three of the hardest closing holes in golf.

name: Dunes Golf and Beach Club
description: A Robert Trent Jones layout on the Grand Strand, best known for the lake-guarded par-5 13th.

name: PGA Frisco (Fields Ranch East)
description: The PGA of America's new home in North Texas, a broad prairie course built for championships.

name: Colonial Country Club
description: Ben Hogan's Alley: a tree-lined Fort Worth classic whose 3rd, 4th and 5th are the Horrible Horseshoe.

name: Muirfield Village Golf Club
description: Jack Nicklaus's tribute to Augusta outside Columbus, with immaculate conditioning and streams through the property.

name: TPC Toronto at Osprey Valley - North Course
description: A heathland-style course at Osprey Valley with sandy waste areas and fescue framing the holes.

name: TPC River Highlands
description: A short Connecticut course that ends on a lakeside run, known for low scores and dramatic finishes.

images.credit: Bröder Media Group from Orrington, ME, USA

name: TPC Deere Run
description: A D.A. Weibring design above the Rock River in Illinois, where birdies come in bunches.

name: The Renaissance Club
description: A Tom Doak links on the East Lothian coast beside the Firth of Forth, used as the warm-up before the Open.

name: Hurstbourne Country Club
description: A Louisville country club with tree-lined fairways and rolling bluegrass terrain.

name: St Andrews Links - Old Course
description: The Home of Golf: double greens, hidden pot bunkers, the Road Hole, and the walk over the Swilcan Bridge.

name: Puntacana Resort & Club - Corales Course
description: A Caribbean course along the cliffs of Punta Cana, finishing on the Devil's Elbow over the sea.

name: TPC Twin Cities
description: An Arnold Palmer design north of Minneapolis with water on many holes and a reachable closing par 5.

name: Silverado Resort - North Course
description: A Napa Valley resort course lined with oaks, with a creek winding through the property.

name: Sedgefield Country Club
description: A 1920s Donald Ross design in Greensboro with crowned greens and tree-lined, rolling fairways.
